mappings.name: demo: a confirm that will DECLINE for want of funds, armed by MSISDN

why: TWO PARTYID FAMILIES, added Step 9 lane 2b (2026-09-04): `237600000f01` and its
digits-only twin `237600000101`. `f01` carries a hex letter so a WireMock
mapping can key on it -- exactly why it is unusable from a real payer:
`frontends/apps/checkout/src/lib/msisdn.ts` validates Cameroon E.164 (`237` +
`6` + eight DIGITS) and refuses it, as it refuses any other letters
(`docs/plans/step9-notes/lane-3.md` #4c). `237600000101` is what that page's
form actually accepts, in the same `2376000000xx` documentation block, `101`
naming no hex value it could be confused with. The `matches` regex joins both
into the SAME `mtn-demo-decline` scenario rather than forking it, so a payer who
typed a real number gets the identical NOT_ENOUGH_FUNDS walk `237600000f01` has
always gotten. Proven directly by
`a_digits_only_msisdn_reaches_the_same_walk_as_its_hex_twin::case_2_insufficient_funds`
in `backends/tests/conformance/tests/adapter_conformance.rs`, which is also what
makes the GET mapping below's 'no conformance case sends that MSISDN' claim no
longer true for `237600000101` -- corrected there. The full steering table, both
families, is in `docs/plans/step9-notes/lane-2b.md`.
FILE: the outcomes examples/merchant-demo drives that requesttopay-status.json
cannot reach from an end-to-end confirm. Added 2026-09-03 (Step 8, lane A) for
issue #11's 'drives the stub to succeeded and to failed/expired'.
THE PROBLEM THIS FILE SOLVES. requesttopay-status.json keys every decline on the
reference (...0f01 = NOT_ENOUGH_FUNDS, ...0f02 = COULD_NOT_PERFORM_TRANSACTION),
and a confirm CANNOT choose its reference: the handler mints
provider_reference_id with Uuid::new_v4() before committing the charge, and a seam
to fix it from outside would be a code path that exists only outside production
(AGENTS.md's first rule). MTN's status query is a GET carrying no body, so it
cannot be steered there either. The MSISDN is the one field of this exchange that
comes from the merchant's own request -- so, exactly as requesttopay.json's
'a payer the rail does not know' mapping and requesttopay-scenario.json's
'mtn-e2e-poll' already do, the steering happens HERE, on the POST, and is carried
to the status query by SCENARIO STATE. Nothing rewrites stored state in the demo.
NO requiredScenarioState, deliberately. This mapping matches in ANY state and
always transitions to `decline-armed`, which is what makes `just demo-walk`
re-runnable against a container it has already driven once. A mapping that
required `Started` would arm on the first walk and silently fall through to the
catch-all SUCCESSFUL on the second -- a demo reporting a settled payment where it
asserted a decline is the exact false green this repository is written against.
237600000f01 is a documentation MSISDN in the same 2376000000xx block the
conformance charges use (237600000000) and requesttopay.json's decline-at-submit
mapping uses (237600000400). Its `0f01` suffix names the reference-keyed status
mapping it mirrors, so the two can be read together.
202, the ordinary accepted submit, because this mapping exists to MOVE THE
SCENARIO and not to change what a confirm sees: the demo asserts this confirm is
indistinguishable from the settling one right up to the point the worker polls.

mappings.name: demo: the armed decline answers NOT_ENOUGH_FUNDS once, then disarms

why: -> insufficient_funds (vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::mapping::FAILURE_REASONS,
docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md). The same body requesttopay-status.json serves
for reference ...0f01; this one is reachable from a real confirm.
MATCHES ANY REFERENCE, which is what makes it usable at all, so four things keep
it from swallowing anything else:
1. requiredScenarioState. A container starts every scenario in `Started`, and only
the POST above moves this one out of it. Every OTHER conformance case sends
the fixed placeholder 237600000000, which matches neither PartyId family
above, so for them this mapping stays unreachable. Corrected Step 9 lane 2b:
one conformance case now DOES send 237600000101 on purpose --
`a_digits_only_msisdn_reaches_the_same_walk_as_its_hex_twin` -- to prove the
digits-only twin reaches this exact decline from the adapter. That case starts
its own container, same as every other one here, so it does not change what
any other case sees.
2. priority 4 is BELOW the reference-keyed status mappings (priority 1, lower
number wins), so ...0404, ...0f01, ...05aa and the rest keep winning even while
this scenario is armed.
3. priority 4 is ABOVE requesttopay-scenario.json's `mtn-e2e-poll` mappings
(priority 5) and above requesttopay-status.json's catch-all SUCCESSFUL
(priority 10). That ordering is load-bearing: a demo run settles the success
outcome first, which leaves mtn-e2e-poll RESTING in `e2e-settled` answering
SUCCESSFUL to every later status query. Without the 4-beats-5 rule the decline
outcome would be told SUCCESSFUL and the demo would report a payment.
4. newScenarioState `Started` disarms it after ONE answer. FAILED is terminal, so
the worker settles on that first poll and asks nothing more about this charge;
disarming means the next outcome in the walk is not answered by this mapping.
THE COUPLING, STATED: this works because examples/merchant-demo drives its
outcomes STRICTLY SEQUENTIALLY -- each charge reaches a terminal state before the
next confirm is sent. Two MTN outcomes in flight at once against one container
would be two charges sharing one scenario, and the wrong one could be declined.
The demo says so where it iterates.

mappings.name: demo: a confirm whose PROMPT WILL EXPIRE, armed by MSISDN

why: TWO PARTYID FAMILIES, added Step 9 lane 2b (2026-09-04): `237600000f02` and its
digits-only twin `237600000102`, for the same reason and by the same mechanism
as the decline pair's mapping above (`237600000f01`/`237600000101`) -- see that
mapping's comment for the full explanation. Proven directly by
`a_digits_only_msisdn_reaches_the_same_walk_as_its_hex_twin::case_3_payer_timeout`
in `backends/tests/conformance/tests/adapter_conformance.rs`. The full steering
table, both families, is in `docs/plans/step9-notes/lane-2b.md`.
The prompt-expiry outcome: the payer never entered their PIN and MTN's ~5 minute
window closed. Same mechanism, same justification and the same documentation-MSISDN
block as the decline pair above; `0f02` names requesttopay-status.json's
reference-keyed equivalent.
IT IS NOT SPELLED `EXPIRED`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `EXPIRED` is ORANGE's status
string (orange/mappings/transactionstatus.json, -> payer_timeout). MTN documents no
`EXPIRED`: its status vocabulary is PENDING / SUCCESSFUL / FAILED, and the reason on
a FAILED prompt that timed out is COULD_NOT_PERFORM_TRANSACTION -- which is exactly
the row vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::mapping::FAILURE_REASONS annotates 'The payer never
entered their PIN; MTN gives them about five minutes'. Inventing an MTN `EXPIRED`
to make the two rails look alike would be this stub asserting something about a
rail nobody has called. Both outcomes still land on the SAME core code,
payer_timeout, which is the thing a merchant integrates against.

mappings.name: demo: the armed expiry answers COULD_NOT_PERFORM_TRANSACTION once, then disarms

reason.message: The transaction could not be performed

why: -> payer_timeout. The OBJECT-shaped `reason`, mirroring requesttopay-status.json's
...0f02 mapping: MTN documents both a bare string and this object, and the
adapter must read either (mapping::failure_code, fed by the `Reason` enum in wire.rs). The decline mapping above
uses the string shape, so one demo run exercises both readings over the wire.
The four properties that keep the mapping above from swallowing anything else
apply here unchanged, and so does the strictly-sequential coupling.

mappings.name: demo: a confirm the RAIL WILL NOT ANSWER FOR, armed by MSISDN

why: Added 2026-09-06 (exp22) so examples/shop's test-number panel can reach
`provider_unavailable` -- the 'the rail is unavailable' outcome the demo
is required to show, and the one outcome above that neither of the two
existing pairs produces.
DIGITS ONLY, and no hex twin. The two pairs above carry both a
`237600000f0x` family and a digits-only `2376000001xx` one, because the
hex spellings predate the checkout page's MSISDN validator and had to be
kept working. This number is new, so it is only ever the digits-only
form a payer can actually type
(frontends/apps/checkout/src/lib/msisdn.ts refuses letters). `503` names
the HTTP status the outcome reads as, which is a mnemonic and nothing
more: the mapping below answers 200 with a FAILED body, because that is
what MTN documents.
202, the ordinary accepted submit, for the reason the pairs above give:
this mapping exists to MOVE THE SCENARIO, and the confirm must be
indistinguishable from a settling one right up to the point the worker
polls.
No requiredScenarioState, and the same strictly-sequential coupling: see
the decline pair's comment above, which explains all four properties in
full.

mappings.name: demo: the armed unavailable answers SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE once, then disarms

why: -> provider_unavailable (vpay_adapter_mtn_momo::mapping::FAILURE_REASONS,
docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md). MTN's own word for it, taken from the
nine-row table the adapter transcribes -- not invented here.
IT IS A 200 WITH A FAILED BODY, NOT A 503, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE
POINT. An HTTP 5xx from the status query is a TRANSPORT failure: the poll
ladder retries it, for hours, and the charge stays pending -- which is
right, and which is not an outcome a demo can show in a minute. A
documented `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` reason on a FAILED status is the rail
SAYING it could not serve this charge, which is terminal and is what a
merchant integrates against.
The four properties that keep the decline mapping above from swallowing
anything else apply here unchanged: priority 4 is below the
reference-keyed status mappings and above the catch-all, the scenario
starts in `Started` in every container, and one answer disarms it.
